Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $y,$ we have the following properties:

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-8-(-3) \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $x,$ we have the following properties:

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x$

In our case, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ -{\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ -16 & =-11+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\ -5 & ={\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x=-5.
$$

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ is the path comprising of a quarter circle of radius $3$ and a line segment, as shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${y}_{1}=1$ and ${y}_{2}=-4.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1}=(-4)-1=-5.
$$

questions.problem: Calculate ${∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the closed path along a circle of radius $2,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.
questions.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${y}_{1}={y}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y=0.
$$
